about.title: Santa Cruz Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Whether you work in agriculture, tourism, construction, or one of the shops along Soquel Avenue and Ocean Street, a workplace injury in Santa Cruz can throw your income and recovery into question fast. California generally requires injured workers to go through workers' compensation rather than suing an employer directly, but that's not always the end of the story. If a subcontractor, equipment manufacturer, property owner, or another driver on Rt 1 or Water Street contributed to what happened, you may have a separate claim against that third party, on top of any comp benefits. We handle workplace injury claims directly and can sort out whether workers' comp is your only path or if there's more to pursue. There's no cost for a consultation, and no pressure to move forward if it's not the right fit.

whyChoose.title: Why Santa Cruz Workers Choose Us

items.title: Third-Party Claims Aren't Automatically Ruled Out
items.desc: Workers' comp is usually the exclusive remedy against your employer, but a negligent third party — like a subcontractor or equipment maker — can still be held separately liable. We can help determine if that applies to your situation.

items.title: Reporting Deadlines Matter Early On
items.desc: California generally requires reporting a workplace injury to your employer within 30 days, and missing that window can complicate things. Getting guidance sooner rather than later helps protect your options.

items.title: Retaliation Protections Exist Under California Law
items.desc: It's illegal for an employer to retaliate against you for reporting an injury or filing a claim. If you're worried about that, we can explain your rights before you decide how to proceed.

items.question: I was hurt on a job site near Soquel Avenue — can I sue my employer directly?
items.answer: In most cases, California workers' comp is the exclusive remedy against your employer regardless of who was at fault, so a direct lawsuit against the employer usually isn't available. However, if a third party like a contractor, equipment supplier, or another driver contributed to the injury, a separate claim against that party may be possible. We can look at the specifics of your job site incident to sort this out.

items.question: What if my injury happened while driving for work on Rt 1 or Ocean Street?
items.answer: If you were injured in a work-related vehicle collision, workers' comp typically applies, but if another driver caused the crash, you may also have a third-party injury claim against that driver. These claims generally carry a 2-year deadline in California, so it helps to get guidance early. We handle both angles and can review your case at no cost.

items.question: Can my employer fire me for reporting a workplace injury in Santa Cruz?
items.answer: No — California law prohibits retaliation against employees who report a workplace injury or file a workers' comp claim. If you believe you've faced retaliation, that's worth discussing with an attorney right away. Contact us for a free consultation to discuss your situation.
